content.content:
Haj-Wan: "I wait for Sei-Wan, my kin. He walked out into the basin alone, to prove himself to the Agaceph, and he has not come back. I am Agaceph too. By our custom none of us may follow a walk-out, so I stay at this gate. An outsider may follow him. He went east from the gate through the shallows, and he is up among the roots there. Vipers lie in the roots, and the mud holds anyone who stands still. Nothing that walks in the basin lives long. Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden beside me, will say the same. I want him alive. He wants the walk-out to count, and it counts only if he comes home on his own feet. If another brings him in, the Agaceph will say he did not finish. I would have him alive and shamed sooner than proud and dead. Bring him home if you must. But if he can walk, let the walk-out be his own."

- Haj-Wan, waiting beside Gih-Xaleel, the levy warden at Helstrom's gate, told me her kin Sei-Wan walked out into the basin alone to prove himself to his tribe, the Agaceph. He has not come back. By their custom the Agaceph may not follow him, but an outsider may. He went east from the gate through the shallows. I'm to find him up among the roots there.
- The viper in the roots of the shallows east of Helstrom's gate is dead, and Sei-Wan can come down from the roots. Haj-Wan wants him home alive, but he wants the walk-out to be his own. I can talk him home, which costs him the walk-out, or tell him to walk home on his own feet and say nothing at the gate. I'm to speak to Sei-Wan among the roots and choose.
- I told Sei-Wan to walk home on his own feet and left him among the roots in the shallows east of Helstrom's gate, and I said nothing of it to Haj-Wan. His walk-out stays his own. Haj-Wan keeps waiting at the gate and knows nothing.

input.command: /tmp/ptb-inaz_mik/play end --take 'Short and pleasant. Wandering Helstrom''s NPCs gave mostly flavour and directions, and I had no lead until I tried Haj-Wan, the silent one at the gate. Her quest about Sei-Wan was well set up: a real dilemma between her wish to have him home and his pride in the walk-out. I had already killed the viper at the start, which made the problem resolve neatly, though it was luck. I chose to let him walk home and stay silent, and it felt like a considered, humane choice. Weak points: the opening gave no direction, so I only found the quest because I talked to everyone; most topics are generic; the duplicated persuade option was odd. I would like to see what comes next in Helstrom and Stormhold, but the quest ended without a follow-up.'

content.text:
I finished the one quest I found, "The Gates of Helstrom", and my journal has no active objectives left, so I ended the session with my take.

- **The quest:** Haj-Wan, waiting at the gate, asked me to find her kin Sei-Wan, who had walked out into the basin alone to prove himself to the Agaceph tribe. I found him stuck up in the roots east of the gate.
- **The viper:** The viper he was afraid of was the one I had already killed at the start of the game, so that part resolved itself.
- **My choice:** I could have talked him home, which would have cost him the walk-out. Instead I told him to walk home on his own feet, and I promised to say nothing at the gate. Haj-Wan still doesn't know.
- **What I noticed:** The opening gave no direction. I only found the quest by talking to everyone in Helstrom. Most dialogue topics were generic flavour and directions. The "Persuade" option on Sei-Wan appeared twice with the same text. The quest ended with no follow-up.
